items.title: Dual-feature selectivity enables bidirectional coding in visual cortical neurons
items.why: Uses deep-learning digital twins of macaque V1/V4 neurons to run in silico experiments, then relates the findings to recordings in two species. This is a strong example of a predictive model generating testable hypotheses about biology. It is the peer-reviewed Version of Record, and the eLife assessment rates the evidence compelling.
items.takeaway: The authors report that many visual cortex neurons are tuned to both an enhancing and a suppressing feature.

items.title: Aggregate Deep Visual Proteomics reveals selective organization of α-synuclein inclusions
items.by: Oeller, M.; Vasconez Grunauer, S.; Sitron, C. S.; Mahul Mellier, A.-L.; Diedrich, L.; Schuele, A.; Ruf, V.; Oliinyk, D.; Kuttler, F.; Dransfeld, U.; Prassler, J
items.why: Profiles laser-microdissected α-synuclein inclusions against the rest of the same cell by mass spectrometry, across a cell line, iPSC-derived neurons and post-mortem brain. It frames three competing views of what inclusions are as different predictions about their composition. This is a bioRxiv preprint and is not peer reviewed.
items.takeaway: The authors report that inclusions concentrate a selective subset of the cell's proteome, including whole protein complexes.

items.title: Scalable methylome-transcriptome profiling resolves clonal organization in human hematopoiesis
items.by: Shao, J.; Chen, M.; Liu, Y.; Sun, J.; Zhang, G.; Yan, Z.-Y.; Lin, H.; Ren, M.; Pei, S.; Peng, J.; Gong, Y.; Wang, S.-W.
items.why: Presents a joint methylome and transcriptome single-cell method, Droplet-MT, that uses methylation epimutations to reconstruct clones in human blood and leukemia. It is a useful look at a single-cell multi-omics design. This is a preprint, and the authors declare a patent application and company affiliations.
items.takeaway: Reference-based label transfer assigns cells to established clones at about 0.2% CpG coverage, which lowers sequencing cost.

items.title: Health-System-Wide Mapping of Demographic Information in Routine Clinical Histopathology
items.by: Shengjia Chen, Ruchika Verma, Kevin Clare, Paula Restrepo, Jannes Jegminat, Eugenia Alleva, Kuan-lin Huang, Aryeh Stock, Brandon Veremis, Thomas Fuchs, Gabriele
items.why: Maps how well sex, age group and self-reported race can be recovered from routine H&E slides using pathology foundation models, across 1.3 million slides and 25 organs. It is directly relevant to shortcut learning and evaluating computational pathology models. This is an arXiv preprint.
items.takeaway: The authors report that demographic signal is broadly detectable, with pan-organ mean AUROCs of 0.828 for sex, 0.733 for age group and 0.662 for self-reported race.

items.title: Continuous diffusion language models
items.why: Sander Dieleman updates his earlier diffusion language model writing, covering why continuous diffusion faded after 2023 and why it is returning. It explains embeddings, losses, noise schedules and self-conditioning for categorical data. The author describes it as a subjective account.
items.takeaway: He suggests the late-2023 shift to discrete methods may reflect a focus on matching autoregressive performance at scale, but he calls this speculative.

items.title: Species Have Blurry Boundaries
items.why: Traces how protein and rRNA sequence comparisons reshaped bacterial taxonomy, and why horizontal gene transfer blurs species boundaries. It is a careful essay on how to interpret genomic evidence in evolution and microbiology. The excerpt is partial, so the rest of the argument is unchecked.
items.takeaway: Genes from the same genome can yield trees with different topologies, which complicates species boundaries such as the ≥95% ANI cutoff.

items.title: A Gentle Introduction to Graph Neural Networks
items.why: A visual, interactive build-up of graph neural networks, including molecules as graphs and graph-, node- and edge-level tasks.
items.takeaway: The article moves from a bare-bones implementation to a modern GNN, explaining the design choices at each step.

items.title: Weight Banding
items.why: A short interpretability study of 'weight banding' in the last conv layer of vision models. It tests causes through interventions such as rotating the dataset and removing global average pooling. The Distill authors note the finding is not yet actionable.
items.takeaway: Banding appeared in InceptionV1, ResNet50 and VGG19 but not AlexNet, and removing pooling eliminated it in the simplified model.

earlier.title: Diffusion language models
earlier.why: The earlier Dieleman post on diffusion language models.

earlier.title: Neural Networks, Types, and Functional Programming
earlier.why: A Colah essay that maps representations to types and common network patterns (RNNs as folds, conv layers as windowed maps) onto functional programming.
earlier.takeaway: The author says openly that this is an aesthetic, speculative argument that is probably wrong, but worth discussing.

earlier.title: Self-Organising Textures
earlier.why: Connects Turing-style reaction-diffusion pattern formation in biology to neural cellular automata trained for texture synthesis. It shows how a PDE is discretised into a learned local rule. It also supplies code and notebooks.
earlier.takeaway: The article argues that numerically discretising a general PDE over image space is equivalent to a neural cellular automaton.

earlier.title: Information-Driven Design of Imaging Systems
earlier.why: A blog post on estimating mutual information from noisy measurements to evaluate and optimise imaging systems, including microscopy, without training a decoder. The post links to a NeurIPS 2025 paper and code; the results are the authors' own.
earlier.takeaway: The authors report that their information estimate tracked downstream performance across four imaging domains, and that optimising it matched end-to-end design in color filter tests.

earlier.title: The First OpenBind Blind Challenge
earlier.why: Announces a prospective, blind protein-ligand pose-prediction challenge on Zika NS2B-NS3 protease, with stricter success criteria than the usual 2 Å RMSD threshold. It is a concrete way to compare docking and cofolding methods without retrospective leakage. The interim deadline (11 Nov) is imminent and the final deadline is 16 December.
earlier.takeaway: Success requires 1.5 Å RMSD, lDDT-PLI above 0.8, and passing PoseBusters validity checks.

earlier.title: Verifiability
earlier.why: A short opinion piece arguing that verifiability, meaning whether a task can be reset, attempted many times and automatically rewarded, predicts where AI progress is fast. It offers a useful lens for scientific ML, where experimental validation is the bottleneck. It is a personal framing, not an empirical result.
